> 聖人常無心，以百姓心為心。善者，吾善之；不善者，吾亦善之，德善.

Chapter 48 was subtraction: reduce until non-forcing remains.

Chapter 49 asks what a person looks like, standing among others, after that subtraction.

Three characters in the chapter are all not what we usually read.

## 歙 is an inhalation

歙: 縮鼻也 — to draw in through the nose. A breath inward.

## 注 is a channel pouring

注: 灌也 — water channeled into one place. 百姓皆注其耳目: the people pour their eyes and ears outward, all of them into the same channel.

## 孩 is a child's laugh

孩: 小兒笑也 — the laugh of a small child.

Which makes the last two lines a single respiration:

The people pour out through eyes and ears until they are exhausted. The sage draws inward — 歙歙焉 — and gives back a laugh.

## 聖人常無心

The sage has no fixed 心. Not "no heart," not "empty of feeling": 無心 means no standing standard carried inward — no fixed measure that everything arriving must be checked against.

The usual reading of 以百姓心為心 is that the sage follows the people. That is not what the sentence says. Following would still require one standard — the people's — applied uniformly.

> 以百姓心為心 is: he does not carry one ruler and measure everyone with it. Each person's heart is met as itself.

## 善者，吾善之；不善者，吾亦善之

> 善者，吾善之；不善者，吾亦善之，德善.

The good, I treat as good; the not-good, I also treat as good. That is 德善.

This is routinely read as moral generosity: be kind to everyone. But the chapter has just removed the fixed standard, and generosity would restore it.

Read with 無心: the second 善 is not approval. It is not slotting the not-good person into a lower rank and being nice about it.

It is: the treatment is the same because the ranking was never applied.

德善 — the 善 that comes from 德 rather than from judgment. Same for 信: 信者，吾信之；不信者，吾亦信之，德信.

## 為天下渾其心

> 聖人在天下，歙歙焉，為天下渾其心.

He draws in, and for the world he keeps his heart 渾 — undifferentiated, like turbid water not yet settled.

渾 is not confusion. It is the state before division: the water that holds everything and has not sorted it into clean and unclean.

This is the chapter's inner counterpart to chapter 15's 混兮其若濁. The reason he can meet each heart as itself is that he has not sorted them.

## 百姓皆注其耳目，聖人皆孩之

The people pour out through eyes and ears; the sage gives them back a child's laugh.

The image is precise about direction. The people's attention is all outflow — looking, listening, chasing. The sage's response is not another outflow; it is 孩之, a laugh.

Why a laugh and not a teaching? Because a teaching would be another channel for them to pour into. A laugh closes the circuit: it returns them to themselves without giving them a new object.
